assessment: In this manuscript, Lawrence et al. investigate the direct effects of the microtubule-associated protein, Sjögren's Syndrome Nuclear Autoantigen 1 (SSNA1), on microtubule dynamics and damage using purified proteins and TIRF microscopy. The authors show that SSNA1 is a microtubule stabilizing protein that acts to slow rates of growth and shrinkage, and promote rescue. Furthermore, SSNA1 serves as a sensor of microtubule damage and protects microtubules from the microtubule severing enzyme, spastin. This paper will be of broad interest to scientists interested in cytoskeletal cell biology.
